categories.tagline: Almanac's threads, made easier to search, steer and trust once you have a few hundred of them.

categories.name: Almanac's Grimoire of Tools
categories.tagline: More kinds of tools behind Almanac's IToolSource, and a clearer look at what the model did with them.

categories.name: Almanac's Proving Grounds
categories.tagline: Benchmark and model-fit work, so players can see what their card can really run beside the game.

categories.name: Almanac at the Adventurer's Side
categories.tagline: Ways for Almanac to fit around actual play: duties, spoilers, busy hands and repeated questions.

ideas.title: Search Every Thread
ideas.pitch: A search box over every conversation you have had with Almanac, so the answer from last Tuesday is two keystrokes away instead of lost in the sidebar.
ideas.experience: You remember asking which Bozjan zone had the fish you wanted, but not when. Type 'bozja fish' in the thread sidebar and three hits appear with the matching line highlighted. Click one and the thread opens scrolled to that message.
ideas.how: Add an FTS5 virtual table over messages.content in AlmanacStore's schema (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS beside threads/messages), kept in step by triggers so AppendMessage, ForkThread and DeleteThread need no changes. A new AlmanacStore.Search(query) returns (thread id, seq, snippet). ChatWindow.DrawThreads gets an input above 'New thread'; ChatSession.Open grows a seq to scroll to. Tool results are indexed but ranked below user and assistant lines.
ideas.risks: FTS5 has to be present in the e_sqlite3 the plugin ships and loads inside Dalamud; SqliteNativeTests should assert it the way it asserts the version. The first open on an existing database has to backfill the index, which must not block the framework thread. Prompted-mode tool results are stored as user messages with PromptedTools.ResultPrefix and need filtering.
ideas.audience: everyone who uses the chat regularly

ideas.title: Context Gauge
ideas.pitch: A small bar in the chat header that shows how full the model's context is, and trims old tool output before it overflows instead of after.
ideas.experience: Twenty questions into a crafting session the gauge turns amber. Hover it: 'about 6,900 of 8,192 tokens; the recipe dump from step 3 is 2,100 of them'. Almanac shortens that old result on the next turn and says so in a yellow notice line.
ideas.how: ChatSession.Window cuts to the last 40 messages (HistoryWindow) whatever their size, so one large get_recipe result can fill a small context. ChatResult already carries PromptTokens; read the served context length from Ollama's /api/show or the gateway, store it per model next to model_caps, and replace the message-count window with a token budget that trims old tool output first, as the engine's [agent] context_tokens does. ChatWindow.DrawHeader draws the gauge.
ideas.risks: Not every server reports prompt tokens or its context length, so the gauge needs an honest 'unknown' state and a character-count estimate. Trimming a tool result the model still needs makes it call the tool again or guess. Prompted mode puts the tool list in the system prompt, which counts too.
ideas.audience: players on 8 GB cards and small-context models

ideas.title: Answers You Can Click
ideas.pitch: Map coordinates, item names and duty names in a reply become small buttons that place the flag or show the details, without asking the model again.
ideas.experience: Almanac answers 'The Summoning Bell is at X 11.2 Y 14.5 in Old Gridania'. The coordinates are underlined; click them and the flag lands on your map. Hover 'Grade 8 Tincture of Strength' and a card shows its ilvl and where you already have some.
ideas.how: Structured tool results (ToolOutcome.Json, kept in CallRecord) already name the zones, items and coordinates the answer was built from, so matching the reply against those is more reliable than parsing free text. ChatWindow's LineKind.Assistant branch renders spans instead of one TextUnformatted. Clicks call engine.XivMcpToolsAsync() then McpToolSource.CallAsync("set_map_flag" | "get_item" | "find_owned_items") directly, going through XivMcp's normal tiers.
ideas.risks: Wrapped ImGui text with inline buttons is fiddly and costs frame time on long transcripts. A model that invents coordinates would get a flag in the wrong place, so only values that came out of a tool result become links. Old threads reopened from SQLite have lost the in-memory CallRecords unless tool JSON is re-parsed from the stored messages.
ideas.audience: everyone, especially new players

ideas.title: A Voice per Thread
ideas.pitch: Give each thread its own system prompt, so the crafting thread stays terse and the lore thread can talk like a Sharlayan librarian.
ideas.experience: Right-click a thread, choose 'Voice', pick 'Crafting tutor'. From then on that thread answers with macros and numbers only, while the story thread next to it keeps its long-winded scholar. Branching a thread keeps its voice.
ideas.how: AlmanacSettings.SystemPrompt is one global string and Engine.GetChatSession passes a Func<string> for it. Store a per-thread prompt in the kv table (thread.<id>.prompt) so no migration is needed, have ChatSession.SendAsync ask for the thread's prompt before the global one, and copy it in AlmanacStore.ForkThread. A few built-in voices ship beside DefaultSystemPrompt; the thread context menu in ChatWindow.DrawThreads picks one.
ideas.risks: A voice that drops the default prompt's rules ('do not guess such facts', 'if an action is denied, do not retry') makes a small model worse at tools, so custom voices should be appended to those rules, not replace them. Voices that imitate named NPCs are fan content; keep the shipped ones generic.
ideas.audience: roleplayers, crafters, anyone with several long-running threads

ideas.title: Export a Thread for a Bug Report
ideas.pitch: Save a thread as Markdown with its tool calls, model and settings, after a review step that blanks out names and tokens.
ideas.experience: The model called the wrong tool twice. Right-click the thread, 'Export for a report'. A preview shows the transcript with your character name, retainer names and the XivMcp endpoint replaced by placeholders; you untick one line you would rather keep private and save the file.
ideas.how: AlmanacStore.Messages(threadId) already returns every message with tool calls and tool results. ChatSession.Render is the model for turning them into lines. Add a header with Engine.Version, engine.ModelLabel, ToolMode and ToolProfile, run a redaction pass seeded from get_player's result and the settings' URLs and tokens, and show the result in a window with per-line exclusion before writing it next to the plugin config directory.
ideas.risks: Redaction by string match will miss things, such as a friend's name in a chat log a tool returned; the review step is the real safeguard and the README's warning about unreviewed transcripts still applies. The export must never include LeaderboardToken, AlmanacToken or XivMcpToken.
ideas.audience: bug reporters, benchmark contributors, the maintainer

ideas.title: Sandboxed WebAssembly Tools
ideas.pitch: Let players add small tools, such as a gil calculator or a rotation lookup, as WebAssembly modules that can reach nothing they are not granted.
ideas.experience: You drop tincture-math.wasm into Almanac's tools folder. Settings lists it with 'no filesystem, no network'. Ask 'how many tinctures for a week of savage at two pulls an hour?' and the chat shows '→ tincture_math' with the answer worked out by code, not guessed by the model.
ideas.how: The WasmToolSource sketched in ToolSources.cs's doc comment: one module per tool, exporting its ToolDef JSON and call(args-json) -> result-json, run under WASI with no preopens or sockets by default. It only has to implement IToolSource; Engine.NewLoop adds it to the ToolHub list after XivMcp, so XivMcp keeps name priority. Per-module grants shown in SettingsWindow; the runtime is disposed in Engine.Dispose and counted by LiveObjects so the reload leak tests cover it.
ideas.risks: A Wasm runtime such as Wasmtime brings a native library that has to load inside Dalamud on Windows and under Wine, the same class of problem as the SQLite native library, and must unload cleanly on plugin reload. Fuel or time limits are needed so a looping module cannot stall a turn. Sharing modules invites people to run code from strangers; grants must default to nothing.
ideas.audience: tinkerers, theorycrafters, plugin authors

ideas.title: Your Own Notes as a Tool
ideas.pitch: Point Almanac at a folder of Markdown notes, such as your glamour plans, retainer ventures or static's strats, and the model can search them in game.
ideas.experience: Ask 'what did we decide for the tank swap on P3?' and the chat shows '→ notes_search tank swap P3', then quotes the two lines from static-strats.md with the file name, instead of making something up.
ideas.how: A NotesToolSource implementing IToolSource with two read-only tools, notes_search and notes_read, backed by an FTS5 index in almanac.sqlite (the Python engine's knowledge base does the same with SQLite FTS5, so its front-matter format can be reused). Engine.NewLoop adds it to the ToolHub list; ToolProfiles gains the two names in SmallSet so small models see it. Re-index on a file-change watcher or on a Refresh button in SettingsWindow.
ideas.risks: Notes go to whatever model server is configured, which may not be local; the settings page has to say that. A large folder makes results long and eats a small context (see the context gauge). A file watcher under Wine on a Z: path may not fire, so manual refresh has to exist anyway.
ideas.audience: raiders, crafters, organised players, FC officers

ideas.title: The Engine's Knowledge in Game
ideas.pitch: When the plugin already uses an Almanac gateway, also offer the engine's read-only tools, such as kb_search and model_residency, in the in-game chat.
ideas.experience: Your homelab notes live in the engine's knowledge base. Mid-queue you ask 'is the NAS backup still failing?' and the in-game chat calls almanac__kb_search and host_status through the engine, while game questions still go to XivMcp.
ideas.how: ToolHub already merges several sources, first-lister wins. When AlmanacSettings.Engine == EngineAlmanac, create a second McpToolSource over McpHttpClient pointed at the engine's MCP port (41880) with AlmanacToken and id "almanac", and add it after XivMcp in Engine.NewLoop. Filter to tools whose safety is read, since the engine's change tools rely on MCP elicitation or confirm tokens the chat window does not implement.
ideas.risks: The engine's gateway and MCP server are separate listeners with the same bearer token; a player who exposed one but not the other gets a confusing half-connection. Tool names may collide with XivMcp's, so the engine's need a prefix. Engine tools that run commands on remote hosts should stay out of the in-game list even if marked read.
ideas.audience: engine users, homelab players

ideas.title: Tool Call Inspector
ideas.pitch: Click any grey tool line in the transcript to see the full arguments and result, how long it took, and whether the call passed schema validation.
ideas.experience: The answer about tomorrow's weather looks wrong. Click '← get_weather_forecast (0.4s)' and a panel opens with the formatted JSON: the model asked for the wrong territory id. Copy the call, or rerun it as it was to check the tool itself.
ideas.how: ChatSession.Shorten cuts tool lines to 120 characters and Render throws the rest away. Keep the StoredMessage seq on tool lines (it is already there), and on click load the full message from AlmanacStore.Messages, pretty-print it with System.Text.Json, and pair each call with its result by ToolCallId. Validation reasons come from Scorer.Validate as AgentLoop already records them in CallRecord. Rerun is only offered for tools in the read tier.
ideas.risks: Tool results can be large, such as a full inventory, and drawing them every frame in ImGui is slow unless the text is cached and clipped. Prompted-mode threads store calls as plain assistant text, so pairing needs the PromptedTools parser. Rerunning an action-tier call must never be possible from here.
ideas.audience: players testing models, benchmark contributors, plugin developers

ideas.title: Only the Tools the Question Needs
ideas.pitch: Before each turn, narrow the offered tools to the few that fit the question, so small models stop reaching for get_equipment when you asked about the weather.
ideas.experience: With the full tool set a 4B model used to call three unrelated tools before answering. Now the header reads 'tools: 5 of 38 for this question'. It asks get_weather_forecast once and answers.
ideas.how: ToolProfiles' own comment says small models do better with fewer tools; today the choice is a static small/standard/all set. Add a per-turn filter to ToolHub: score each ToolDef by keyword overlap and, where the server offers one, embeddings from an /v1/embeddings model, keep the top N plus a fixed core (get_location, get_player). Measure it with BenchRunner against the unfiltered sets before it becomes a default.
ideas.risks: Leaving out the tool a question needed is worse than offering too many: the model guesses. Embeddings need a second model loaded next to the chat model and the game. Changing the tool list between turns of one thread can confuse models that cache tool names, and it makes benchmark results incomparable unless recorded in the result.
ideas.audience: players on small models and 8 GB cards

ideas.title: Answers Back Over IPC
ideas.pitch: A second IPC version that lets another plugin ask Almanac a question and receive the reply as it streams, not only open the chat window.
ideas.experience: A terminal plugin's /ask panel or a desktop widget shows Almanac's answer in its own bubble, word by word, with tool lines in grey, and the Almanac window never opens.
ideas.how: Plugin.cs registers Almanac.ApiVersion (1) and Almanac.Ask (Func<string, bool>), which only opens ChatWindow and calls Send. Add ApiVersion 2 with Almanac.AskInThread returning a request id, and an Almanac.Event IPC message carrying the same events ChatSession.OnEvent already handles (TextDeltaEvent, ToolStartedEvent, ToolFinishedEvent, done or error), serialised like the engine's --stream-json lines. Requests run in their own ChatSession so they do not fight the window's thread.
ideas.risks: Two ChatSessions against one local model double the load; requests need a queue and a busy answer. IPC messages are delivered on the caller's thread and a slow subscriber could stall streaming. Any plugin can call it, so it must not accept a system prompt or tool profile from the caller.
ideas.audience: plugin authors, Ghostty and XivDesktop users

ideas.title: Head to Head
ideas.pitch: Pick two past benchmark runs and see them side by side, task by task, with the tool calls each model made.
ideas.experience: Past runs lists qwen3.5:9b at 0.81 and a newer 8B at 0.78. Tick both and press Compare: they tie on location and weather, the 8B fails flag_coordinates by swapping X and Y, and it answers 0.4 s sooner on average. Now you know which one to keep.
ideas.how: Every run is already in bench_runs with its full ResultJson (AlmanacStore.BenchRuns returns BenchRow). BenchmarkWindow's 'Past runs' header gets checkboxes and a Compare table built from the per-task entries in each result, with columns for tool validity, answer check and time to first token. Only runs with the same SuiteVersion are comparable; others are shown greyed with the reason.
ideas.risks: Results from different context sizes, quantisations or mock versus live mode look comparable and are not, so the table must show those settings at the top. Old result JSON written before a schema change needs tolerant parsing.
ideas.audience: players choosing a model, leaderboard contributors

ideas.title: Context Fit Finder
ideas.pitch: A wizard step that tries the chosen model at 8k, 16k and 32k context, measures VRAM and speed at each, and recommends the largest that does not spill into system RAM.
ideas.experience: The wizard says your 12 GB card has about 8.5 GB left beside the game. Press 'Find my fit': three short runs later it reports 32k spills and drops to 4 tok/s, 16k fits at 31 tok/s, and it sets 16k for you.
ideas.how: SetupWindow already computes the VRAM budget (GpuInfo, GameReserveMb) and Engine.BenchRunnerAsync builds a runner with an IVramProbe (OllamaVramProbe first, NvidiaSmiProbe as fallback) sampled by VramSampler. Run a three-task subset of Suite.Bundled() with Ollama's num_ctx option per step, record peak VRAM and tok/s, and detect spill as a sharp drop in speed or Ollama reporting size_vram below size.
ideas.risks: Only Ollama takes a per-request context size; LM Studio and llama.cpp fix it at load time, so for them this can only advise. Each step reloads the model, which takes time and briefly competes with the game for VRAM. Under Wine, nvidia-smi may not be reachable from inside the game.
ideas.audience: new players, anyone sharing one GPU with the game

ideas.title: Headroom Gauge
ideas.pitch: A live readout of VRAM used by the game and the model, and of the last reply's tokens per second, so you can see a hub or a busy FATE pushing the model out.
ideas.experience: In a quiet field the small gauge in the chat header shows 2.1 GB free. You enter Limsa at peak hour and it drops to 300 MB; the last reply took 9 s at 6 tok/s. Almanac suggests the small tool set and a lower context until you leave.
ideas.how: Reuse IVramProbe from Bench/Vram.cs on a slow timer (every few seconds, off the framework thread), plus DXGI's QueryVideoMemoryInfo next to the adapter enumeration in GpuInfo.cs for the game's own budget. Tokens per second come from ChatResult's OutputTokens and elapsed time, already measured for the benchmark. ChatWindow.DrawHeader shows it; thresholds come from GameReserveMb.
ideas.risks: QueryVideoMemoryInfo through DXVK under Wine may report numbers that do not match the real card. nvidia-smi polling costs a process spawn each time; keep it slow or use the Ollama probe. Numbers that jump about will worry people more than help them, so smoothing matters.
ideas.audience: players on 8-12 GB cards, benchmark contributors

ideas.title: Turn a Conversation into a Benchmark Task
ideas.pitch: When a model gets a real question badly wrong, turn that exchange into a proposed benchmark task, with the tool results frozen as fixtures, for the next suite version.
ideas.experience: The model told you the wrong aetheryte for a hunt mark. Right-click the question, 'Propose as a benchmark task'. A form shows the prompt, the tools that were needed, their results captured as fixtures and a field for the correct answer; you submit it for review instead of just grumbling.
ideas.how: A thread already holds the user prompt, each tool call and its JSON result, which are the shape of a SuiteTask (Prompt, Tools, Expect) and of the suite's fixtures that FixtureToolSource replays. Build the draft task from AlmanacStore.Messages, let the player write the Expect rules in the vocabulary JsonRules and Scorer already use, and send it through the existing DeviceLink sign-in to a proposals endpoint, not straight into ffxiv-core.
ideas.risks: Fixtures captured live contain the character name, location history, retainers and possibly other players' names from chat tools; the form has to redact them and show the exact payload, as Share does. Every accepted task changes the suite's Sha256 and breaks comparability with past runs, so tasks must batch into versioned releases. Writing good Expect rules is hard for most players.
ideas.audience: benchmark contributors, the leaderboard's maintainers

ideas.title: Quiet While You Pull
ideas.pitch: Almanac hides its window in combat and duties, holds any reply that finishes meanwhile, and tells you with a toast once you are out.
ideas.experience: You asked about a recipe just before the queue popped. The window slides away at the barrier. Twenty minutes later the boss dies, and a quiet toast says 'Almanac: your answer about Rarefied Sykon Bavarois is ready'. /almanac opens it where you left off.
ideas.how: Inject ICondition and IToastGui into the Plugin constructor beside ICommandManager and IFramework. On IFramework.Update, watch ConditionFlag.InCombat and BoundByDuty; set ChatWindow.IsOpen false and remember it was open. ChatSession keeps running on the thread pool as it does now; when it goes from Busy to idle during quiet mode, queue one toast for when the flags clear. A setting in SettingsWindow turns it off.
ideas.risks: Some players want the window open in duties, such as for a crafting-log duty or a trial they have cleared many times, so it must be optional. Toast wording should not look like a game system message. Condition flags change briefly during cutscenes and zone loads and need a short debounce.
ideas.audience: raiders, roulette players, anyone who asks questions in queue

ideas.title: Give the VRAM Back for Duties
ideas.pitch: When the model shares the game's GPU, unload it as you enter a duty and load it again when you leave, so savage frame rates do not pay for an idle chatbot.
ideas.experience: Enter the raid and a small notice says 'Almanac released 5.8 GB for the duty'. You wipe, you clear, you leave; by the time you are back at the Summoning Bell the model is warm again and your first question answers without a cold start.
ideas.how: Only when AlmanacSettings.GameOnSameGpu is set. For an Ollama backend (BackendKind), POST /api/generate with keep_alive 0 on BoundByDuty and a no-prompt load with keep_alive -1 on leaving, the same calls the engine's residency loop makes. The ServerDetector root URL and Engine.Quick HttpClient already exist for this. Skip it while ChatSession is Busy, and show the state in the chat header.
ideas.risks: With the Almanac gateway as the engine, its own residency loop pins the model while ffxiv_dx11.exe runs and will fight the plugin, so the gateway needs a way to be told, or the plugin must stay out of it. LM Studio and llama.cpp have no equivalent API. Reloading a model right as the duty ends causes a stutter in town; a delay helps.
ideas.audience: raiders on single-GPU machines, players on 8-12 GB cards

ideas.title: Spoiler Guard
ideas.pitch: Almanac checks how far you are in the main scenario and keeps its answers about lore, NPCs and later zones behind that line unless you ask it not to.
ideas.experience: Midway through Heavensward you ask who a certain knight is. Almanac answers with what you have already seen, then adds: 'There is more about him later in the story. Ask again with /almanac spoilers on if you want it.'
ideas.how: At the start of a thread, and when the zone changes, call XivMcp's get_quest_status for a short list of main scenario milestones and put the furthest completed one into the system prompt that ChatSession builds each turn, with a rule not to reveal later events. A toggle in settings and a /almanac spoilers on|off subcommand in Plugin.OnCommand. Answers based on search_quests or get_quest for quests beyond that point get a warning line.
ideas.risks: A local model's own training is the main source of spoilers and a prompt rule will not stop all of them; this lowers the risk and must say so. Choosing the milestone list takes knowledge of the story and upkeep every patch. Players on a new character may have finished the story on another.
ideas.audience: new and returning players, story-focused players

ideas.title: Reference Pages
ideas.pitch: Save a question you ask often as a named page and run it with one command or macro line, so your daily checks are one keypress.
ideas.experience: Every evening you type the same three questions. Now /almanac page evening runs 'which retainers are back, what is the weather in Eureka Pagos for the next hour, and which of my gathering tokens are close to the cap?' and puts the answer in its own thread.
ideas.how: Store pages in the kv table under page.<name>. Plugin.OnCommand gains a 'page <name>' case that opens a fresh thread through ChatSession.New and sends the stored text via ChatWindow.Send. A small list in SettingsWindow edits them, and the transcript's context menu gets 'Save this question as a page'. Because it is a slash command it can sit in a game macro.
ideas.risks: A page that asks for an action-tier tool will still stop for XivMcp's approval, which is correct but surprising in a macro. Pages run one at a time; a second while Busy is refused, as Almanac.Ask is today. It must never become a timer that runs itself.
ideas.audience: daily-routine players, gatherers, crafters

ideas.title: Push to Talk, Read Aloud
ideas.pitch: Hold a key, ask your question out loud, and hear the answer spoken, with speech recognition and voice both running on your own machine.
ideas.experience: Both hands are on the controller mid-gathering. You hold the chosen key and say 'when does the next ephemeral node spawn here?'. The words appear in the chat window as you speak, the tool line flickers, and a quiet voice answers while you keep moving.
ideas.how: Capture microphone audio in the plugin (for example NAudio's WASAPI capture), send it to a local whisper.cpp server's /inference endpoint that ServerDetector could find like the model servers, and pass the text to ChatWindow.Send. For speech, stream the TextDeltaEvent text sentence by sentence to a local TTS server such as Piper and play it on a separate audio device. Settings hold the two endpoints and the key.
ideas.risks: Microphone capture inside the game process under Wine is unreliable, and audio APIs differ per system. Speech recognition and TTS take GPU or CPU next to the chat model and the game, which is exactly the budget the wizard is trying to protect. Picking up voice chat from a party must never happen by accident, so push to talk only, with a clear indicator.
ideas.audience: controller players, gatherers, players who prefer speaking to typing
